chunks.rationale: README.md first (user-facing capability bullets under The rest of the desk / Also in the box / Updates), then docs/ARCHITECTURE.md in heading order: Worktrees (fail-closed, retention/GC, forge probe), Store (Spaces retired), coder-threads MCP (new section), Orchestration commands (#606 palette), Renderer notes + Pane workspace + Build SHA mismatch, Sidebar (native menu, icons, nested workers). The two files are one story: README says what you can do, ARCHITECTURE says where it lives. Diff is additive except the old snooze/pin/shelves README bullet, which described a contract the UI no longer renders.
risks: The hand-off brief listed a single Later shelf (#567) and per-project create clusters. Live UI is buildFlatSidebar (T3-flat): pinned block + snoozed shelf + settled shelf, create options on the header caret. Docs follow the code, not that brief. A reviewer scoring against the brief will think Later is missing.

Pane workspace: only chat and diff are shipped; terminal/browser/files/tasks/subagent are placeholders. ARCHITECTURE says so. Do not read the README Git-as-center-pane bullet as implying Thread|Git header tabs — the header is a Views menu plus onViewChanges hydration.

coder-threads host-tool table is a summary, not the MCP input schemas. thread_merge's default-branch gate vs own-worktree staging is the load-bearing sentence; if that is wrong the docs teach the agent to land on main again.

Issue #560 (archived transcripts not re-stringified) was in the brief as shipped. It is a closed duplicate of still-open #225; store.js still JSON.stringify(this.data) including messagesByThread. Left out on purpose — documenting it as done would be a lie.

Perf-pass issue numbers (#526/#527/#528/#533) are closed but have no user-facing surface worth a README bullet; ARCHITECTURE already described the store debounce that those passes landed on. Nothing new to cite without inventing.
No site/, package.json, or app source was touched. Website worker owns site/.
